brief.headline: KOSPI Circuit Breaker: Samsung -14%, SK Hynix -14% as Broadcom Miss and US Jobs Data Trigger Semis Rout
brief.summary: <cite index="20-11,20-12">Samsung traded at 302,500 won (-13.94% vs Friday's 351,500 won) and SK Hynix at 1.971M won (-14.23% from 2.298M won)</cite> as <cite index="22-8,22-9">KOSPI triggered circuit breakers after plunging 8.37%</cite>. <cite index="22-14">Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plummeted 10.26% Friday—largest drop since March 2020</cite> on <cite index="22-4">Broadcom AI chip sales guidance miss and stronger US nonfarm payrolls fueling Fed rate hike fears</cite>. <cite index="27-4,27-5">NH Investment raised Samsung target to 530k won and SK Hynix to 3.2M won on agentic AI memory demand and rising HBM/DRAM pricing</cite>, but <cite index="22-16,22-17">the pair account for ~50% of KOSPI weight; retail margin debt hit 37.74 trillion won as of June 4</cite>, amplifying liquidation pressure.
brief.pair_trade_view: SK Hynix maintains structural edge: <cite index="6-8">SK Hynix held 53% HBM share in Q3 2025 vs Samsung's 35%</cite> and <cite index="1-18">UBS predicts SK Hynix will capture ~70% HBM4 share on Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026</cite>. <cite index="1-13">Goldman assessed SK Hynix will sustain >50% total HBM share through at least 2026</cite>. Samsung recovering but from weaker base: <cite index="4-39,4-40">Samsung's HBM share plummeted from 41% in Q2 2024 to 17% in Q2 2025 due to Nvidia qualification delays; analysts forecast Samsung strengthens as HBM3E qualifies and HBM4 ramps in 2026</cite>. Near-term, both face identical macro/positioning risk (today's correlation: 0.97), but SK Hynix deserves 15-20% relative premium given <cite index="1-16">partnership with TSMC on packaging, Cheongju M15X fab, and Global AI Research Center</cite>. Long Samsung vs. short SK Hynix 2x leverage ETFs into month-end if spreads compress <10%.

memory_cycle.stage: Late Upcycle with Supply Discipline Lock
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="13-1,13-6">TrendForce revised Q1 2026 DRAM contract prices to +90-95% QoQ (from initial +55-60% estimate), NAND +55-60% QoQ</cite>. <cite index="11-7,11-8">Q2 2026: DRAM contracts +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ following Q1's record 90-95% DRAM surge</cite>. <cite index="14-5,14-6,14-7">Samsung and SK Hynix (70% of global DRAM) signaled no aggressive capacity expansion; pricing rally projected past 2028</cite>. <cite index="10-3,10-5">Samsung and SK Hynix raised HBM3E supply prices ~20% for 2026 as Nvidia H200, Google TPU v7, Amazon Trainium3 shipments begin</cite>. <cite index="1-21,1-22,1-23">HBM investment creates virtuous cycle: supply-demand tightening for general DRAM; institutional investors see server DDR5 and HBM as two pillars in 2026</cite>. Structural: <cite index="14-25">Micron noted 3-to-1 HBM/DDR5 wafer conversion ratio—every HBM ramp compresses commodity memory</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-1,1-10">HBM3E expected to account for ~two-thirds of total HBM shipments in 2026, with HBM4 gradually increasing share</cite>. <cite index="8-6,8-7">LS Securities estimates HBM3E will be 66% of total HBM output in 2026, down from 87% in 2025; inflection with Nvidia Rubin launch in H2 2026</cite>. <cite index="8-11,8-13">Nvidia asked suppliers if they could deliver 16-layer HBM in Q4 2026; performance evaluation expected before Q3 2026</cite>. <cite index="3-3,3-4">SK Hynix's Cheongju M15X fab to complete first cleanroom May 2026, pilot operations begin; facility will manufacture both HBM3E and HBM4</cite>. <cite index="10-8,10-9">HBM content per accelerator rising 20-30%; Google TPU v7 integrates 8 HBM3E stacks, Amazon Trainium3 uses 4 stacks</cite>. Pricing: <cite index="3-9">Some analysts warn HBM prices could enter correction after 2026 as competition heats up and capacity expands</cite>, but <cite index="10-11,10-12">HBM3E supply remains tight as Samsung and SK Hynix prioritize HBM4 ramp; 2026 HBM revenue mix forecast at ~55% HBM4, 45% HBM3E with HBM4 absorbing HBM3E demand from Q3</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI triggers circuit breaker, Samsung -14%, SK Hynix -14% in two-day rout
news_pulse.implication: Forced selling from retail leverage (37.74T won margin debt) and single-stock ETF liquidations (-26% in 2 days) creates technical overhang. Korea Investment suspended margin trading after credit limits exhausted. Near-term capitulation risk if USD/KRW breaks 1,560.

news_pulse.headline: Philadelphia Semiconductor Index -10.26% Friday, worst drop since March 2020
news_pulse.implication: Broadcom AI revenue guidance miss and US 10Y yield >4.5% triggered global semis selloff. Micron, Nvidia, Marvell hammered. Contagion to Korea amplified by 50% KOSPI weight in Samsung/SK Hynix.

news_pulse.headline: NH Investment raises Samsung PT to 530k won, SK Hynix to 3.2M won on agentic AI
news_pulse.implication: Samsung Q2 DRAM ASP +48% QoQ, NAND +60%; SK Hynix DRAM +42.5%, NAND +45%. Agentic AI spreading demand to server DRAM, eSSD, LPDDR SOCAMM beyond HBM. Longer-term contracts reduce volatility, support re-rating.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix raised HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026 contracts
news_pulse.implication: Nvidia H200 (6 HBM3E stacks), Google TPU v7 (8 stacks), Amazon Trainium3 (4 stacks) shipments drive HBM3E ASP gains despite HBM4 ramp. Tight supply as vendors prioritize HBM4 capacity.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex $600B+ in 2026, 75% ($450B) tied to AI infrastructure
news_pulse.implication: Big Five (Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Oracle) AI capex +36% YoY. Memory will consume 30% of hyperscaler datacenter spend in 2026 (4x vs 2023). Structural tailwind for HBM/DDR5/eSSD.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices +90-95% QoQ in Q1 2026, NAND +55-60%—TrendForce revises up
news_pulse.implication: Memory shortage worse than expected. Q2 forecast: DRAM +58-63%, NAND +70-75%. PC DRAM to roughly double from Q4 2025; LPDDR4X/5X +90% QoQ, steepest increases in history. Prices to remain high through 2028.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS-L and CoWoS-S fully booked through 2026; Nvidia secures >60% capacity
news_pulse.implication: Nvidia, Google, Amazon, MediaTek orders drive full CoWoS utilization. AI GPUs/ASICs growing in size (bigger dies, 6-to-8 HBM stacks). TSMC expanding CoWoS-L, reallocating CoWoS-S equipment. HBM demand locked for 12+ months.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia asked suppliers about 16-layer HBM delivery in Q4 2026
news_pulse.implication: Exploratory but accelerates generational transition before 12-layer HBM4 reaches full rollout (still expected early 2026). 16-layer technically harder than 8-to-12 transition; may require manufacturing process changes. Samsung considering hybrid bonding for 16-layer HBM4E.

brief.derivatives_signal: Single-stock leverage ETFs down -26% in 2 days; negative compounding accelerates in volatile tape. Korea Investment suspended margin trading. Retail net bought 2.04T won in KODEX/TIGER SK Hynix leverage ETFs (May 27–Jun 5) now underwater. Options skew likely inverted (puts bid). Watch for gamma unwind if Samsung breaks 300k won or SK Hynix breaks 1.9M won. KOSPI 200 futures gapped limit-down Friday (-8%), rolled into spot Monday. KRW at 1,560/USD—intervention level. Defensive: fade rallies into dealer hedge unwind, or buy 3-month ATM straddles if vol collapses post-circuit-breaker.
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung/SK Hynix stabilization or retest of intraday lows (Samsung 302.5k, SK Hynix 1.971M)—technical support determines whether retail capitulation complete
USD/KRW through 1,560 triggers BOK verbal/physical intervention; foreign outflow acceleration would pressure ADRs in US session
Nvidia partnership announcements with SK Group/LG (data centers, humanoid robots, automotive) mentioned in Korean media—could provide short-term relief bid
Any emergency Financial Services Commission statement on margin debt or ETF trading restrictions; precedent: 2020 COVID circuit breakers led to short-selling bans
US afternoon: Micron, Nvidia, Broadcom price action—if stabilizes, Korea ADRs (SSNLF, HXSCL) could front-run Tuesday open relief rally
